Twelve flags, one per page, so a page can be turned on for a site or pulled back without touching the rest of the module.

- `incidents_dashboard_page`
- `incidents_list_page`
- `incidents_detail_page`
- `incidents_students_page`
- `incidents_employees_page`
- `incidents_vehicles_page`
- `incidents_locations_page`
- `incidents_communications_page`
- `incidents_reports_page`
- `incidents_workflows_page`
- `incidents_admin_page`
- `incidents_help_page`

What a page flag does. Hides the navigation entry and refuses the direct URL, returning the user somewhere sensible rather than a blank page or an error, because anyone holding the link reaches the page otherwise. It also stops the page issuing requests, so a disabled page costs nothing.

Every flag defaults off. Targeting is by site, so a district is wholly on or wholly off for a given page, with no partial state inside the district.

The supported states are all off, all on, and pages enabled one at a time. Two combinations are prevented rather than left to chance: the detail page enabled while the list page is off, which leaves records nobody can navigate to, and the employees or locations page enabled before the subject work is on, which leaves a page with nothing to list.

Acceptance criteria:

- Each of the twelve flags exists with the name above and defaults off.
- With a page flag off, the navigation entry is absent and the direct URL does not render the page.
- With a page flag off, the page issues none of the requests it would normally make.
- Turning a flag on for one site leaves every other site unchanged.
- The detail page enabled with the list page disabled is prevented.
- The employees and locations pages cannot be enabled before the subject work.
- Turning every flag on produces the same application as running with no flags.
title: Feature flag set for the Incidents pages

body:
Sending works and the step configuration already offers the switches, but nothing states which notifications go out, to whom, or what they say. That gap is why the current mails are generic, and it needs to be written down before the templates get invented one at a time.

What triggers a notification. Each is configured per workflow step, so a district turns on what it wants and nothing fires by default.

- The step starts.
- The step completes.
- The step's assignee is notified that it is theirs.
- Approvers are notified that a step is waiting on them.
- Named groups are notified.

Who receives it. The step's assigned role resolves to the people holding that role, plus any approver roles selected on the step, plus any address typed into the step's recipient list. A role with nobody in it sends nothing rather than failing.

There is no variable substitution. The copy below is fixed text, with nothing pulled from the incident, so every mail is a prompt to go and look rather than a carrier of detail.

Action Required, sent to the people holding the step's role.

> Subject: Action required in the Incident Tracker
>
> A workflow step in the Incident Tracker is assigned to your role and needs attention.
>
> Sign in to Incidents and open your assigned incidents to see what is waiting.

Approval Request, sent to the approver roles selected on the step.

> Subject: Approval needed in the Incident Tracker
>
> A workflow step in the Incident Tracker is waiting for your approval.
>
> Sign in to Incidents and open your assigned incidents to approve the step or send it back for revision.

Parent or Guardian Notification, sent to the guardians of a student named on the incident.

> Subject: Transportation incident involving your student
>
> Your student was involved in an incident.
>
> Someone from the transportation team will contact you to go through what happened. If you would like to reach us first, please call the transportation office.
>
> This message does not include details, because they are better discussed directly.

The parent mail carries no student name, no date, no time, no incident type and no severity, and that is the right call twice over. Mail is not a private channel and often lands on a shared account, so specifics belong in the conversation that follows. It also avoids stating a time the module frequently does not have.

The limitation worth being honest about: with no substitution, a coordinator holding three open steps receives three identical mails and cannot tell them apart without signing in. That is tolerable at low volume and it is the reason the incident identifier is the first variable worth adding when substitution arrives.

Parent or Guardian Notification only applies where a student is involved. An Employee, Vehicle, Location or Third Party incident never sends it, whatever a step is configured to do, because there is no guardian to address and a district cannot afford that mail going out about a driver.

Wording per incident type comes later. A step on a weapon incident and a step on a disruptive behavior incident send the same Action Required mail, which is acceptable because the reader opens the incident to act anyway.

Acceptance criteria:

- Each of the five triggers can be turned on and off per step, and is off by default.
- Turning on a trigger sends to the resolved role holders, the selected approver roles, and any typed addresses.
- A role with no holders produces no mail and no error.
- Each of the three templates sends exactly the copy above, with no placeholder text left visible in the subject or the body.
- The parent mail contains no student name, no date, no time, no incident type and no severity.
- Selecting Parent or Guardian Notification on a step of a non-student incident sends nothing.
- A step with no notification configured sends nothing when it starts or completes.
- A sending failure is visible somewhere a coordinator can see that the mail did not go.
title: What notifications the module sends, and what each one says

The Help page is product copy, not code: three tabs holding Getting Started, an eleven section user guide, and twenty one FAQ entries. Development should not have to transcribe it out of a prototype or a screenshot, and product should be able to correct a sentence without touching a component.

The copy lives in three markdown files checked into the repository beside the Help component, one per tab.

- `getting-started.md`, holding the overview, the navigation description, the five incident roles, and the feature cards.
- `user-guide.md`, one heading per section, in the order the accordion shows them: Dashboard, Incident Management, Workflow System, Students, Communications, Vehicles, Employees, Locations, Reports, Admin, Notifications.
- `faq.md`, a flat list where each entry is a heading for the question and the text below it for the answer.

Three files rather than one, because each maps to a tab, so a change to the FAQ cannot disturb the guide. A flat FAQ rather than a nested structure, because adding a question should be adding a heading and a paragraph with no layout to edit. Headings carry the section order, and the component renders headings into accordion items, so the copy holds no markup that implies a layout.

Ownership.

Product owns the wording in these files. Development owns how they render. A wording change arrives as an edit to the file, not as a ticket describing the sentence.

What the copy currently says.

Stated so it is clear what is being handed over: the five subjects and that the subject is chosen first, the two step form, the 20 incident types with their categories, the 12 workflows and the required Incident Owner, the difference between the incident date and the reported date, how the term is derived and that nothing is filtered by term, the twelve location types, the per-column filters and pagination on every grid, and the five incident roles.

It also states plainly that one incident record is created and each person named on it carries their own workflow, which had been described the other way round.

Acceptance criteria:

- Three markdown files exist in the repository, one per Help tab.
- The Help page renders from those files, and no Help copy is hardcoded in the component.
- Every heading in `user-guide.md` appears as a section in the guide, in file order.
- Every question in `faq.md` appears in the FAQ, in file order.
- Editing a sentence in a file and rebuilding changes the rendered page with no component edit.
- Adding a question to `faq.md` adds it to the page with no component edit.
- The rendered Help page describes the five subjects, the two step form, the 20 types, the 12 workflows and the five incident roles, and does not describe a four step wizard, a linked record per student, or seven roles.
title: Hand the Help page copy to development as source files

body:
Each subject needs its own incident types, and each type needs a workflow to run when an incident is filed against it. The two belong together because a workflow is selected by incident type plus severity, so a type without a workflow files an incident that nothing picks up.

The 20 types, by subject.

The list offered on the form is filtered to the chosen subject, and Applies To is a column in Admin so the subject of every type is visible and editable. Each type carries a default severity that fills in on the form and stays overridable.

Student, 6

- Disruptive Behavior, Behavioral, Low
- Safety Violation, Safety, Medium
- Physical Altercation, Aggression / Violence, High
- Property Damage, Property, Medium
- Weapon / Prohibited Items, Prohibited, Critical
- Witness / Bystander Statement, Informational, Low

Employee, 4

- Employee Altercation, Employee Conduct, High
- Employee Misconduct, Employee Conduct, Medium
- Employee Injury, Safety, High
- Employee Substance Violation, Prohibited, Critical

Third Party, 4

- Third Party Collision, Collision, High
- Third Party Injury, Safety, High
- Third Party Conduct, Aggression / Violence, High
- Public Complaint, Informational, Low

Vehicle, 3

- Vehicle Damage, Mechanical, Medium
- Mechanical Failure, Mechanical, Medium
- Single Vehicle Collision, Collision, Medium

Location, 3

- Location Damage, Location, Medium
- Utility Failure, Location, Medium
- Location Safety Hazard, Location, High

Ten categories, and why they are drawn this way.

Behavioral, Safety, Aggression / Violence, Property, Prohibited, Informational, Employee Conduct, Location, Mechanical, Collision.

Category describes what happened, not who it happened to, because category is what the list filters on and what reports group by. The subject already carries who. Three consequences worth stating, since they look inconsistent until the reason is visible:

- Employee Injury sits under Safety rather than Employee Conduct, so a workplace injury does not appear in a conduct report pulled about that person.
- Employee Substance Violation sits under Prohibited alongside Weapon / Prohibited Items, so a district asking how many substance incidents it had gets one number instead of two split by whether a student or an employee was involved.
- Public Complaint sits under Informational, which keeps a parent phoning in a complaint out of the collision count that goes to leadership and insurance.

The 12 workflows.

Every one of the 20 types is covered by exactly one workflow. Selection is by incident type plus severity. Forty-six steps in total.

- WF-001 Disruptive Behavior Response, owner School Principal, 3 steps, Disruptive Behavior at Low
- WF-002 Physical Altercation Response, owner School Principal, 5 steps, Physical Altercation at High
- WF-003 Prohibited Items Response, owner Administrator, 5 steps, Weapon / Prohibited Items at Critical
- WF-004 Property Damage Investigation, owner Administrator, 6 steps, Property Damage at Medium
- WF-005 Safety Violation Response, owner Safety Coordinator, 5 steps, Safety Violation at Medium
- WF-006 Witness / Bystander Statement, owner Safety Coordinator, 1 step, Witness / Bystander Statement at Low
- WF-007 Employee Conduct Review, owner Administrator, 4 steps, Employee Altercation, Employee Misconduct and Employee Substance Violation at Critical, High or Medium
- WF-008 Employee Injury Report, owner Administrator, 3 steps, Employee Injury at Critical, High or Medium
- WF-009 Location Issue Response, owner Administrator, 4 steps, Location Damage, Utility Failure and Location Safety Hazard at any severity
- WF-010 Vehicle Damage and Mechanical Response, owner Fleet Manager, 4 steps, Vehicle Damage, Mechanical Failure and Single Vehicle Collision at any severity
- WF-011 Third Party Incident Response, owner Safety Coordinator, 4 steps, Third Party Collision, Third Party Injury and Third Party Conduct at Critical, High or Medium
- WF-012 Public Complaint Review, owner Safety Coordinator, 2 steps, Public Complaint at Low or Medium

Routing differs by subject on purpose. Employee and location incidents go to an Administrator rather than a school principal, vehicle incidents to a Fleet Manager, third party incidents to a Safety Coordinator. Every step assigns to one of the five incident roles provisioned by #188, being Administrator, Safety Coordinator, Driver, Fleet Manager and School Principal, so no new roles are needed.

Each workflow names a required owner role, which is what gives a filed incident an assignee. The mechanics of assignment and routing are covered by Incident assignment and routing (#197); this ticket covers the type and workflow definitions those mechanics run against.

Acceptance criteria:

- All 20 types exist, each with the category and default severity listed above.
- The type list on the form shows only the types belonging to the chosen subject, verified on all five.
- Admin shows Applies To per type and allows it to be changed.
- Choosing a type fills in its default severity, and the severity remains editable.
- All 12 workflows exist with the owner role and step count listed above.
- Filing an incident on any of the 20 types selects a workflow, with none left unmatched.
- An Employee Injury at High selects WF-008 and not WF-007.
- A Public Complaint selects WF-012 rather than a collision workflow.
- Every step in every workflow assigns to one of the five incident roles.
- A report grouped by category places Employee Injury under Safety and Public Complaint under Informational.
title: The 20 incident types and the 12 workflows that route them

body:
An incident is often filed after the fact. A driver finishes the route, and the report gets written that evening or the next morning. The record has to carry the date and time the incident happened, not the moment someone got around to entering it, because every question anyone asks of the data afterward is about when it happened.

The record therefore holds two separate timestamps, and both are visible on the incident.

Incident date and time. When the incident occurred. Both required.

- The date defaults to the current date.
- The date cannot be set in the future.
- The time starts empty rather than prefilled with the current clock. A prefilled time passes validation while being wrong, which is the exact error this field exists to catch, so the reporter has to enter a value.
- Helper text on the date reads "When the incident occurred, not when you are filing it."
- Helper text on the time reads "Approximate is fine if the exact time is unknown."

Reported date and time. When the record was created. Set by the system, and not editable by any role including Administrator.

Editing an incident later can correct the incident date and time. The reported values never change.

Where the incident date is used. Sorting and date filtering on the incidents list, and any report that groups by day, month or term, all use the incident date, because that is what people mean by when it happened. The reported timestamp is a record-keeping value, not a reporting axis.

Lateness is not a product judgment. There was never a time when incidents were reported at the moment they happened, and what counts as late depends on district policy. The product records both values so a district can answer that against its own policy. Nothing in the interface or in a report flags, badges or counts an incident as late.

Acceptance criteria:

- An incident cannot be submitted without both an incident date and an incident time.
- The date field arrives defaulted to the current date, and the time field arrives empty.
- Choosing a date in the future is rejected with a clear message.
- The incident record displays the incident date and time and the reported date and time as distinct values.
- No role can edit the reported date and time, verified as Administrator.
- Editing an incident changes the incident date and time and leaves the reported values untouched.
- An incident entered the morning after the event shows the previous day as the incident date and the current day as reported.
- The incidents list sorts and filters on the incident date, not the reported date.
- A report grouped by day or month groups on the incident date.
- Nothing in the interface or in any report describes an incident as late or overdue relative to its reported date.
title: Capture when the incident happened, separately from when it was reported

Today every incident is pre-assigned on creation, and the only assignment tool that exists afterwards is Reassign on the dashboard. In the prototype the assignee is hardcoded, `assignedTo: 'Sarah Williams'` at `NewIncidentForm.tsx:615`, so every new incident lands on the same person regardless of subject, type, severity, or school.

## Direction from the Aug 12 review

Round robin across safety coordinators was proposed and rejected. Justin's concern was implementing round robin across the board, and nobody has asked for it.

The pattern that has to be supported instead comes from a real district: one person handles the majority of all incidents, and one specific school routes to a dedicated person on a different workflow.

A middle option was raised and not pursued: assign a type to one or more people and round robin only within that group.

## Design

**The workflow carries the incident owner.** A workflow can be designated to a user, and that user becomes the incident's assignee at creation.

The incident needs one owner from the moment it is created, before any step is in progress. Taking the owner from a step would mean the owner shifts as the workflow advances, which makes an "assigned to me" view unstable, and Reassign already operates on the incident rather than on a step. Because a workflow is already selected by incident type and severity, one assignee per workflow expresses "all of these go to one person" directly, as a single setting rather than one per step.

**Steps stay role-based, with no per-step user override.** Steps already assign to a role, and the role list is the seven members of `IncidentRoleType`, so a district can already say that Disciplinary Review goes to School Principal. A per-step user override would add a second way to assign, create an ambiguity whenever the role and the override disagree, and answer a question nobody has asked. A district that genuinely needs a named person on a specific step creates a second workflow, which is how the district above already handles its one-school exception.

## Requirements

- A workflow can be designated to a user. When an incident is created and that workflow is assigned, the incident's assignee is that user.
- The designated user is validated against active employees. A workflow cannot be pointed at an inactive or deleted employee.
- When a designated user becomes inactive, the behavior is defined rather than discovered: the workflow's designation is cleared and incidents created against it open unassigned into the triage queue, and the condition is surfaced to an administrator.
- A workflow with no designated user creates the incident unassigned.
- Reassign on the dashboard continues to work, and reassigning an incident never changes the workflow's designation.
- Non-student subjects carry no school, so no assignment rule may depend on school without a defined fallback for employee, vehicle, location and third party incidents.

## Known consequence

Workflow selection keys off incident type and severity, not school. A district wanting a school-specific owner has to create a separate workflow for that school, which is what the district above already does. That works, but it means workflow proliferation for every school needing special handling. Recorded as a tradeoff rather than a defect.

## Still open

The instruction from Aug 12 was to find out how that district actually processes and assigns incidents before finalizing this. That discovery is in motion: outreach to Cypress-Fairbanks went out on Aug 19 and a session with their student management leadership is being scheduled. The design above should be confirmed against what that conversation turns up before it is built.
title: Incident assignment and routing

body:
#191 adds Location, Employee, Vehicle and Third Party subjects. The incident list and incident detail handle all four. The entity pages around them do not, so a district can file these incidents but cannot look at them from the other direction.

**1. There is no Locations page, and the affected location is not a real reference.**

Vehicles and Drivers each have a page that lists the entity, shows an incident count, and drills into the incidents behind that count. Locations have neither. A facilities manager cannot ask which depot has the most incidents this year, which is the first question a location subject invites.

Underneath that, the affected location is captured as a name string rather than a reference to a Student Transportation Location. Vehicles already carry a garage LocationId, so the entity exists and the incident is not using it. Until the affected location is a reference, a Locations page cannot be built, and renaming a location silently orphans every incident that named it.

**2. There is no Employees page.**

Drivers is the only people page and it is drivers-only, organized around certifications and their expiry. An aide, a mechanic, or a supervisor who is the subject of an employee incident has no profile and no incident history, so employee incidents will be filed against people who cannot then be looked up.

This does not have to be a new page. Broadening Drivers to all employees with a role filter would cover it, and matches how Student Transportation already treats drivers as employees rather than a separate population.

**3. Drill-through from an incident count is a name search, not an identity filter.**

The incident count on the Drivers and Vehicles grids opens the incidents list with the entity's name pushed in as a free-text search term. That works well enough for a bus number, but it over-matches on people: two employees sharing a surname return each other's incidents, and a location name appearing in any incident description matches too. Every new subject makes this worse, because employee and location incidents are the ones identified by name rather than by a number.

Acceptance criteria.

- An incident's affected location references a Student Transportation Location rather than storing its name.
- A Locations view lists locations with an incident count, and the count opens the incidents behind it.
- Every employee who can be the subject of an employee incident is reachable from a people page, with their incident history.
- Drill-through from any entity's incident count returns only incidents involving that entity, matched by identity rather than by name.

Split out of #191, which owns the subject model itself. The three gaps above are separable and may be worth splitting if they land in different sprints.
title: Secondary pages for the new incident subjects: locations, employees, and drill-through by identity

body:
A workflow step can be marked as requiring approval, but nothing records the outcome of that approval and there is no way to reject.

What exists today.

- `WorkflowInstanceStep.RequiresApproval` flags that a step needs approval.
- `WorkflowStepApproverRole` defines which incident roles may approve a step, at the definition level.
- `WorkflowStepStatusType` has four values: Not Started, In Progress, Complete, Skipped. There is no Pending Approval and no Rejected.
- The only completion evidence on an instance step is `CompletedByEmployeeId`, `CompletedDateUTC` and `Notes`.

Two consequences.

First, an approval is indistinguishable from a completion. When an approver approves a step, the record shows the same fields it would show if the assignee had simply completed it. There is no approver identity and no approval timestamp, so a district cannot answer who approved a disciplinary action.

Second, an approver has no way to reject. The only available actions are approve, which means completing the step, or leave it alone. A step that should go back to its assignee for more information can only stall silently.

Requirement.

- A step that requires approval records the approver, the approval timestamp, and the outcome, separately from who completed the work.
- An approver can reject a step with a required reason. Rejecting returns the step to In Progress, keeps the work already recorded, and notifies the assignee.
- The rejection reason and the rejecting approver persist on the step and appear in the incident history, which #73 already writes.
- A step that was rejected and later approved keeps both events rather than overwriting the first.
- A step pending approval is visibly distinct from one still in progress.

Note on reuse. Student Transportation already has an approval framework in `ApprovalPath`, `ApprovalPathLevel` and `ApprovalPathLevelApprover`, currently unrelated to incident workflow steps. Worth deciding whether incidents adopt it rather than adding approval columns to `WorkflowInstanceStep`, since a district that already configures approval paths elsewhere will expect them to behave the same way.

Found while answering the Help page content audit on #139.
title: Workflow step approval has no recorded outcome and no reject path

Follow up to transportation-traversa#19960, covering blocks 2 and 3 of #181. The work is in the Security DB seeding procs, so delivery lands in transportation-traversa. 19960 stays as approved and these changes go in a new PR.

## 1. Resource tree

`incident-drivers` is renamed to `incident-employees`. In Student Transportation a driver is an Employee, so a separate driver resource would overlap the Employee subject that #191 introduces. The resource is seeded with no grants and is not yet enforced, so the rename carries no data impact.

`incident-locations` is added as a new subject resource for the Location subject.

Acceptance criteria:

- `incident-employees` exists in place of `incident-drivers`, nested under the `incidents` parent
- `incident-locations` exists, nested under the `incidents` parent
- Both carry `ResourcePermissionProperty` entries consistent with the other subject resources
- Both appear in the role permission tree under the `IncidentManagement` upgrade and are hidden when the upgrade is off
- Permission labels are present in `Permission.resx` and the es-US, fr-CA and ar-SA locale files
- Seeding remains additive, `NOT EXISTS` guarded, and re-runnable

## 2. Grants for the subject areas

19960 leaves the subject areas and `incident-admin` ungranted. Combined with the enforcement in #181, ungranted means no role can reach those areas, so defaults are required.

- `incident-students`: Admin full, Safety full, Principal read, Fleet none, Driver none
- `incident-employees`: Admin full, Safety full, Fleet read, Principal none, Driver none
- `incident-vehicles`: Admin full, Fleet full, Safety read and update, Principal none, Driver none
- `incident-locations`: Admin full, Safety full, Principal read, Fleet none, Driver none
- `incident-admin`: Admin full, all other roles none

These are shipped defaults that districts change in the role editor.

Delete is Administrator only, and no other role receives it for any subject area. Deleting an incident removes it from view rather than removing the row: it drops out of lists, counts, search and reports, while the record and its history are retained, and the deletion itself is written to the audit trail with the user and the time.

Acceptance criteria:

- A tenant with the upgrade enabled has the grants above after the permission seed runs
- Each of the five default roles reaches exactly the areas listed and no others
- Re-running the seed adds no duplicate grants
- Existing grants are never edited or removed
- No role other than Administrator holds delete on any incident subject area

## Out of scope

- Application enforcement of the resources, covered by #181
- Third party subject resources, deferred until a Student Transportation entity exists for third party
- Running `InsertDefaultIncidentPermission` at upgrade enable, tracked separately
title: Seed follow up: expand the incident permission resources and grant the subject areas

body:
Accept an incident submitted from a Tyler Drive tablet and create it as a full incident record, with several involved students on one incident, photo evidence, and triage for a submission that cannot be matched to known records.

This issue is the spec of record for the Tyler Drive crossover and covers the Incidents side. The tablet application work is delivered under tyler-technologies/tyler-drive-maui#366. The submit endpoint and configuration are delivered under tyler-technologies/tyler-drive-api#140.

V1 is a driver filing an incident from the tablet, for every subject. A driver facing incident list, incident detail, and driver to coordinator messaging are not in V1.

## What already exists and is reused

- Several involved students on one incident. `NewIncidentStep` runs InvolvedStudents, IncidentDetails, PerStudentDetails, ReviewAndSubmit, and `IncidentDetail` carries a `StudentWorkflows` collection holding one workflow instance per student
- Attachments. `AttachmentService` over `S3AttachmentStorage` behind `IAttachmentStorage`, `IncidentAttachmentRecord`, and `AttachmentUploadValidator` enforcing max size, an extension allowlist, and executable detection
- `AttachmentFileType.Photo`, and `IncidentDetail` keeping `Photos` separate from `Documents`

## 1. Accept a submission and create the incident

- One submission creates one incident. The driver who submitted it is the reporter
- Subject is one of Student, Employee, Vehicle, Location, or Third Party, using the names established in #191
- Incident type and severity arrive as submitted. Severity is defaulted from the type on the tablet and is editable there, so the submitted value is authoritative
- The incident date and time are stored separately from the submission time
- Run, vehicle, driver, school, and grade context captured silently by the tablet is stored on the incident
- The GPS pin and the on a run indicator are stored on the incident
- The incident is assigned its workflow on creation and enters it immediately, identical to an incident created in the web app
- An incident created from a tablet is indistinguishable from a web created incident everywhere except its recorded source

Acceptance criteria:

- A submission for each of the five subjects creates an incident with every submitted field mapped
- The incident appears in the list, in search, and in dashboard counts subject to existing permission and school based filtering
- The incident is on its assigned workflow with the first step live
- Incident date and time are queryable independently of the submission time
- The GPS pin renders on the incident the same way a web entered location does
- The source of the incident is recorded and reportable

## 2. Several involved students on one submission

- The submission carries a collection of involved students, not a single student
- Each involved student carries their own role of Participant, Witness, Reporter, or Injured, plus their own severity, statement, and action taken
- All of them land on one incident, with one `StudentWorkflows` instance per student, matching what the web app creates today
- A submission with one student behaves identically to a submission with several

Acceptance criteria:

- A submission naming three students creates one incident with three involved students, not three incidents
- Each involved student has their own role, severity, statement, and action taken on the record
- One workflow instance exists per involved student
- School based access resolves against every involved student, so a user with access to any one of their schools sees the incident, unchanged from #190
- A submission naming one student creates one incident with one involved student

## 3. Photo evidence

- Photos captured on the tablet arrive with the submission and are stored through the existing attachment service
- They are recorded as `AttachmentFileType.Photo` and appear on the incident's Photos tab
- The same validation the web upload applies is applied to a tablet photo, including max size, extension allowlist, and executable detection
- A photo that fails validation is rejected individually and recorded as such. It does not fail the incident

Acceptance criteria:

- A photo taken on the tablet is present on the resulting incident and viewable on the Photos tab
- Several photos on one submission all arrive
- An oversized or disallowed file is rejected and the incident is still created, with the rejection visible to the coordinator
- A photo is never silently dropped

## 4. Triage for an unmatched submission

- A submission whose student, employee, or vehicle cannot be matched to a known record still creates the incident
- The unmatched values are retained exactly as submitted so a coordinator can resolve them
- The incident is surfaced as needing triage rather than failing or being held
- Losing a driver's report is worse than holding a partial one

Acceptance criteria:

- A submission with an unmatched subject creates an incident and does not error to the tablet
- The submitted values that could not be matched are visible on the incident
- Incidents needing triage are findable as a set, not one at a time
- Resolving the match completes the incident without re-entry
- Photos and the GPS pin survive on an incident that needed triage

## Out of scope

- The driver facing incident list, incident detail, and driver to coordinator messaging. `DriverMEssageController` and `CannedResponseController` already exist in `tyler-drive-api`, so most of the plumbing for messaging is in place when it is picked up
- An authoring UI for the form definitions. Definitions are loaded per tenant, covered under tyler-technologies/tyler-drive-api#140
- Any change to existing conduct form submissions or their FTP and CSV delivery, which continue to work unchanged

## Dependencies

- tyler-technologies/tyler-drive-api#140 delivers the submit endpoint the tablet posts to and the form definitions
- tyler-technologies/tyler-drive-maui#366 delivers the tablet application work, including the involved student collection
- #191 establishes the subject names used here
- #181 and #193 define the permission model that governs who sees a tablet created incident, including the Driver role defaults

body:
An incident is not always about a student. Two employees in a fight has no student. A bus damaged in the yard with nobody aboard has no student. A burst pipe in the depot has no student. A collision with another motorist has no student. STA and Cypress Fairbanks have both asked whether Incidents can be used for non-student events, so a student cannot be a required part of an incident.

This is the parent issue for that change. It covers the subject model, the new incident types and workflows, the date and time capture, and the reorganized create form.

Subjects.

Every incident has exactly one subject. The subject is what the incident is fundamentally about. It determines which incident types are offered, which filing steps appear, which workflow is assigned, and how the record is labeled in the list and on the detail page. There are five:

- Student. One or more students involved. Requires at least one named student.
- Vehicle. Bus damage or a mechanical problem with nobody aboard. Names an affected vehicle, no people.
- Location. A depot, garage, or yard problem such as a burst pipe or power loss. Names an affected location, no people. Location is the entity Student Transportation already uses for a garage or depot, so the subject, its category, and its types all use that word rather than Facility.
- Third Party. Another motorist, a pedestrian, a parent, or a member of the public. Requires at least one named person.
- Employee. Employees only, such as a dispute between drivers or an injured aide. Requires at least one named employee.

Access to an incident is governed the same way for every subject. There is no per-subject visibility rule and employee incidents are not restricted as a class. Who can see an incident is decided by the resource grants defined in #181, applied identically to all five subjects.

Incident types.

The incident type list is filtered by subject, so a vehicle incident only offers vehicle types. The type list has to cover all five subjects, so types and categories are defined for each below. Category describes what happened, not who was involved, because category is what the list filters on and what reports group by. The subject field already carries the relationship.

- Employee: Employee Altercation and Employee Misconduct under a new Employee Conduct category, Employee Substance Violation under the Prohibited category, Employee Injury under the Safety category.
- Location: Location Damage, Utility Failure, and Location Safety Hazard under a new Location category.
- Vehicle: Vehicle Damage and Mechanical Failure under a new Mechanical category, Single Vehicle Collision under a new Collision category.
- Third Party: Third Party Collision under Collision, Third Party Injury under Safety, Third Party Conduct under the Aggression / Violence category, Public Complaint under the Informational category.

Employee Injury is not a conduct matter, so filing it under Employee Conduct would put a workplace injury into any conduct report pulled about that person. Employee Substance Violation sits under Prohibited alongside Weapon / Prohibited Items so that a district asking how many substance incidents they had gets one number rather than two split by whether a student or an employee was involved. Public Complaint under Informational keeps a parent phoning in a complaint out of the collision count that goes to leadership and insurance.

Workflows.

Each new type needs a default workflow. Workflow assignment keys off incident type plus severity, so these types need no new assignment logic. Routing differs by subject:

- Employee incidents assign to Administrator rather than a school principal. An employee matter is not a school discipline matter.
- Location incidents assign to Administrator. They should not reuse the Property Damage workflow, because the response and the approver are different.
- Vehicle incidents assign to Fleet Manager. Nobody was aboard, so there are no statements to collect and the workflow is shorter.
- Third Party incidents assign to Safety Coordinator, and run the steps needed for an outside party, including any claim or insurance follow-up.

Steps assign to the five incident roles provisioned by #188: Driver, Safety Coordinator, Administrator, Fleet Manager, and School Principal. Roles attach to Student Transportation employees through `EmployeeIncidentRole`, and each role has a security group seeded by `InsertDefaultIncidentPermission`, so #188 stays a five GUID procedure. A district that wants a different owner for employee or location incidents reassigns the step in the workflow builder, the same as any other step.

Date and time.

An incident filed the next morning has to carry the date it happened, not the date it was filed. The record therefore needs two timestamps, both visible on the incident.

- Incident date. When the incident occurred. Required. Defaults to today and cannot be set in the future. Helper text reads "When the incident occurred, not when you are filing it."
- Incident time. Required. Not defaulted, so the reporter enters the value. Helper text reads "Approximate is fine if the exact time is unknown."
- Reported date and time. When the record was created. Set by the system and not editable.

Time is required because an AM run and a PM run are materially different events in transportation, time of day is the dimension any route or run based analysis needs, and it is what gives the gap between incident time and reported time any meaning. The reporter entering a historical incident from paper is asked on screen for a best estimate rather than a precise claim, which is what the helper text is for.

Incident list sorting, date filters, and reports that group by day or month all use the incident date, because that is what users mean by when. The gap between the two timestamps is what makes late reporting visible, so the detail page shows both rather than collapsing them into one.

New incident form layout.

The form is reorganized around the subject rather than assuming a student. Choosing the subject comes first, before any other field. It has to, because the subject determines every field that follows. All five subjects are shown together so the whole choice is visible at once.

Every subject then runs the same two steps: Incident Details, then Review and Submit. One form serves all five.

Counted from the form, the Incident Details step carries 17 distinct fields, and 12 are identical for all five subjects: incident type, severity, description, date, time, location type, location on the map, witnesses, third parties, tags, photo evidence, and document evidence.

Five vary, all governed by one map rather than by per-subject screens. People roster, on Student, Employee and Third Party. Affected asset, on Vehicle and Location, the only genuinely subject-specific field and one control whose label and source change. Vehicle Number, absent on Vehicle because the affected asset already names the bus, and absent on Location. Driver, absent on Location. Run, absent on Vehicle since nobody is aboard, and absent on Location.

The per-subject delta from the shared set is therefore Student 4, Employee 4, Third Party 4, Vehicle 2, Location 1. This is one form with a field map, not five forms, which is what makes it a single estimable item rather than a redesign of every screen.

Three rules follow from that. A field never changes position between subjects, so Incident Type sits in the same slot on all five. Fields are one ordered list flowed into a grid, so a field the subject does not need is not rendered and the fields after it close up, leaving no gap where an unused field would sit. People Involved is a section inside Incident Details rather than a step of its own, with per-person detail as an expandable row, and there is one roster implementation rather than one for students and a parallel one for everyone else.

The roster is labeled by subject: Involved Students, Involved Employees, or Involved People.

Field order follows the order a reporter thinks in: who, then what, then when and where, then supporting detail.

Changing the subject after starting a report clears only the subject-specific answers, the incident type, the people involved, and the affected asset, and keeps date, time, description, location, and evidence. The reporter is warned first, so a mid-report switch is never a silent data loss.

Named people carry a role of Participant, Witness, Reporter, or Injured, and a per-person severity, description, action taken, and notes.

People who are present but are not the subject, witnesses and third parties on any subject, carry a name, a phone, an email, and a description. Not every one of them can be named. A person loitering at a stop, or a motorist who drove off, has to be filable as a description alone. A contact is therefore kept when it has either a name or a description, and dropped only when both are empty. Name is required where it is meaningful, which is the subject of the incident: a student, an employee, or a named third party.

Incidents list and detail.

The incidents list replaces its Student column with an Involved column that names whoever or whatever the incident is about, and adds Subject as a sortable, filterable column. Without a subject filter there is no way to isolate location incidents or to pull a student view that excludes employee records, which several acceptance criteria below depend on.

Incident detail shows an Involved Parties section for employee and third party incidents, and an Affected Location or Affected Vehicle card for the two people-free subjects.

School filtering.

Non-student incidents are not filtered by school. This matches the decision in #190 that drivers and vehicles are out of scope for school-based access.

One implementation note. The school filter matches an incident when at least one of its students attends a school the user can access. An incident with no students fails that test, so it would resolve to visible to nobody. Studentless incidents need to bypass the school filter rather than be evaluated by it.

A known tradeoff comes with that. Non-student subjects carry no school scoping of any kind, because drivers have no school foreign key and vehicles carry only a garage LocationId. A user with full employee incident access therefore sees every employee incident district wide. Garage or department scoping would be new architecture and is not in this issue.

Acceptance criteria.

- A Vehicle incident saves with an affected vehicle, no people, and no validation error, and its filing flow shows the same two steps as every other subject.
- A Location incident saves with an affected location, no people, and no validation error, and its filing flow shows the same two steps as every other subject.
- A witness or third party can be saved with a description and no name, and is dropped only when name and description are both empty.
- An Employee incident saves with one or more employees, and is visible to exactly the users its resource grants allow, with no additional restriction applied for being an employee incident.
- A Third Party incident saves with one or more named outside people.
- All five subjects show the same two steps, and Incident Type appears in the same position on all five.
- The incident type dropdown only offers types matching the chosen subject.
- Each new incident type is assigned its workflow on creation, and its steps can be completed and approved the same as a student incident.
- Incident date and incident time are both required, and the Incident Details step cannot be completed without both.
- Incident date cannot be set to a future date.
- Reported date and time cannot be edited by any role.
- Incident list sorting and date filters operate on the incident date.
- The incidents list shows Subject as a column and can be filtered to a single subject.
- Changing subject mid-report clears type, people, and asset, keeps date, time, description, location, and evidence, and warns first.
- The incidents list, incident detail, dashboard, and reports render every subject with no blank subject and no null error.
- A user with access to a single school still sees Vehicle, Location, Third Party, and Employee incidents.

## Summary

When the `IncidentManagement` upgrade is enabled for a tenant, DevOps runs Justin's `InsertDefaultIncidentPermission` (Security DB) which creates the five Incident Groups and returns their GUIDs. We need a companion stored procedure in the Core DB that accepts those GUIDs and sets up the role references in step templates and workflows.

## Background

See https://github.com/tyler-technologies/transportation-traversa/pull/19960

## DevOps provisioning flow

1. Run `InsertDefaultIncidentPermission` (Security DB) - creates Groups, returns GUIDs
2. Run our new Core DB proc with those GUIDs

## What the proc needs to do

The following SQL is being removed from `Script.PostDeployment.sql` as a separate task. The new stored proc must replicate what it did, but accepting role GUIDs as parameters instead of looking up `IncidentRoleType` ids.

The proc should accept five GUID parameters (Administrator, Safety Coordinator, Driver, Fleet Manager, School Principal) and be idempotent (`IF NOT EXISTS` guards).

### SQL being removed

Role id lookups (these become the proc's GUID parameters):

```sql
declare @rDriver    int = (select IncidentRoleTypeId from IncidentRoleType where TypeCode = 1)
declare @rSafety    int = (select IncidentRoleTypeId from IncidentRoleType where TypeCode = 2)
declare @rAdmin     int = (select IncidentRoleTypeId from IncidentRoleType where TypeCode = 3)
declare @rFleet     int = (select IncidentRoleTypeId from IncidentRoleType where TypeCode = 4)
declare @rPrincipal int = (select IncidentRoleTypeId from IncidentRoleType where TypeCode = 6)
```

Step template assigned roles:

```sql
-- Parent/Guardian Notification -> Safety Coordinator
-- Photo & Evidence Documentation -> Driver
-- Disciplinary Review -> School Principal
-- Law Enforcement Contact -> Administrator
-- Documentation & Close -> Safety Coordinator
insert into WorkflowStepTemplate (..., DefaultIncidentRoleTypeId, ...)
values (..., @rSafety, ...)  -- etc per template
```

Step template notify roles:

```sql
insert into WorkflowStepTemplateNotifyIncidentRole (WorkflowStepTemplateId, IncidentRoleTypeId, ...)
select st.WorkflowStepTemplateId, @rSafety, ...
from WorkflowStepTemplate st where st.Name = 'Disciplinary Review'
```

Default workflow steps (Disruptive Behavior Response, Physical Altercation Response, Prohibited Items Response, Property Damage Investigation, Safety Violation Response) - each workflow's steps reference roles via `DefaultIncidentRoleTypeId`:

```sql
insert into WorkflowStep (WorkflowId, DefaultIncidentRoleTypeId, ...) values
((...), @rDriver, ...),   -- step 1
((...), @rSafety, ...),   -- step 2
...
```

Workflow step notify and approver roles:

```sql
insert into WorkflowStepNotifyIncidentRole (WorkflowStepId, IncidentRoleTypeId, ...)
select ws.WorkflowStepId, @rSafety, ... where ws.Seq = 4

insert into WorkflowStepApproverRole (WorkflowStepId, IncidentRoleTypeId, ...)
select ws.WorkflowStepId, @rAdmin, ... where ws.Seq = 4
```

## Context

- Related to transportation-traversa PR #19960 (`feature/develop/94-incident-tracker-permissions`)
- Part of the broader Incidents roles and permissions work
title: Create Core DB stored procedure for seeding Incident role GUIDs into step templates and workflows

Sub-issue of #93. One of 4 report cards on the Reports page (`Transportation.Incidents/Pages/Reports.razor` — currently a header-only stub).

## Report card

- **Title:** Open Incidents Report
- **Icon:** `description`
- **Card description:** "All currently open incidents requiring action"
- Clicking the card / **View Report** opens the report preview modal.

## Data scope / filter

- Filter on status only: `dbo.Status.TypeCode IN (1, 2)` — Open or In Progress — joined via `dbo.IncidentEvent.StatusId`.
- Sort: `dbo.IncidentEvent.AddDateUTC` **descending** (newest first).
- No date-window and no severity filter.

## Columns and their source tables

Data source: `_traversaContext.IncidentEvents` projected through the existing `IncidentEventQueryExtensions.ProjectToRecords()` (returns `IncidentRecord`). All 8 columns are already populated by that projection — only the status filter is new.

- **Incident ID** — `dbo.IncidentEvent.IncidentEventId`. Display as `INC-{id}` via `DisplayHelper.GetIncidentIdDisplayString()`.
- **Date** — `dbo.IncidentEvent.AddDateUTC` (`DATETIME`, stored UTC). Convert to user local, format `MM-DD-YYYY`.
- **Student** — `dbo.IncidentEventStudent.StudentFirstName` + `StudentLastName` and `StudentUniqueId` (snapshot columns on the join row); live student is `IncidentEventStudent.StudentId` → `dbo.Student.StudentId`.
- **Type** — `dbo.IncidentEventType.IncidentName`, joined via `dbo.IncidentEvent.IncidentEventTypeId`.
- **Vehicle** — `dbo.IncidentEvent.AssetName` / `AssetUniqueId` (snapshot); live vehicle is `IncidentEvent.AssetId` → `dbo.Asset.AssetId`.
- **Driver** — `dbo.IncidentEventEmployee.FirstName` + `LastName` where `IncidentEventEmployeeInvolvementTypeId` → `dbo.IncidentEventEmployeeInvolvementType.TypeCode = 2` (Driver); live employee via `EmployeeId` → `dbo.Employee.EmployeeId`.
- **Severity** — `dbo.Severity.TypeName` via `dbo.IncidentEvent.SeverityId`. `TypeCode`: 1 Low, 2 Medium, 3 High, 4 Critical. Forge badge.
- **Status** — `dbo.Status.Name` via `dbo.IncidentEvent.StatusId`. `TypeCode`: 1 Open, 2 In Progress, 3 Closed. Forge badge.

Strong candidates to add for this report (all available on the same query — this is a work-queue report): **Assigned To** — `dbo.IncidentEventEmployee.FirstName` + `LastName` where involvement `TypeCode = 3` (Assignee); **Current Workflow Step** and **Progress (x/y)** — `dbo.IncidentEventStudent` → `dbo.WorkflowInstance` → `dbo.WorkflowInstanceStep` (`Name`, `Seq`, `Status.TypeCode`; `WorkflowStepStatusType.InProgress` = current step, count of `Completed` / total = progress); **Days Open** — computed from `IncidentEvent.AddDateUTC`.

## Preview modal

- Report title as H2.
- **Download Report** primary button; **Excel** and **CSV** export options.
- Scrollable table with the 8 columns above.
- Footer: record count + generated-on date.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Report card renders in the Reports page grid with the title, icon and description above.
- [ ] Only incidents with status Open or In Progress appear, newest first.
- [ ] Status badge theming matches the incidents list (`statusTheme()` pattern).
- [ ] Footer shows correct record count and generated date.
- [ ] Excel and CSV export match the preview rows/columns.
- [ ] Empty state when no open incidents exist.

## Open questions

- Include the Assigned To / Current Step / Days Open columns in v1, or keep the shared 8-column layout across all four reports for consistency?
- Should this be capped to a date window, or all-time open incidents?
- Multi-student incidents: one row per student vs. comma-joined names — keep consistent across all four reports.
- PDF vs. Excel/CSV for v1.

- **Title:** Monthly Summary
- **Icon:** `calendar_today`
- **Card description:** "Incident statistics and trends for the current month"
- Clicking the card / **View Report** opens the report preview modal.

## Data scope / filter

- All incidents whose event date falls in the rolling window **from the same calendar day of the previous month through now**.
- `dbo.IncidentEvent.AddDateUTC >= DATEADD(MONTH, -1, @nowUtc)` (converted to the user's local day boundary — see `CurrentWeekHelper` for the existing UTC-offset pattern).
- Sort: `AddDateUTC` **descending** (newest first).
- No severity or status filter — all severities, all statuses.

## Columns and their source tables

Data source: `_traversaContext.IncidentEvents` projected through the existing `IncidentEventQueryExtensions.ProjectToRecords()` (returns `IncidentRecord`). All 8 columns below are already populated by that projection — no new projection needed, only the date filter.

- **Incident ID** — `dbo.IncidentEvent.IncidentEventId`. Display as `INC-{id}` via `DisplayHelper.GetIncidentIdDisplayString()`.
- **Date** — `dbo.IncidentEvent.AddDateUTC` (`DATETIME`, stored UTC). Convert to user local, format `MM-DD-YYYY`.
- **Student** — `dbo.IncidentEventStudent.StudentFirstName` + `StudentLastName` (name) and `StudentUniqueId` (the STU- id). These are denormalized snapshot columns on the join row; live student record is `dbo.IncidentEventStudent.StudentId` → `dbo.Student.StudentId`. Implement the Incidents Tracker permission model against the resources seeded by transportation-traversa#19960.

That PR seeds the resource tree, five default roles, and 56 grants. This issue covers enforcing them in the application, completing the tree for the expanded incident subjects, and setting grant defaults for the subject areas the PR left ungranted.

Three blocks. Each carries its own acceptance criteria and is estimated separately. Blocks 2 and 3 are changes to the Security DB seeding procs and are delivered under #193.

## 1. Enforce the seeded resources

Resources seeded under the `incidents` parent: `incident-dashboard`, `incident-list`, `incident-students`, `incident-drivers`, `incident-vehicles`, `incident-admin`, `incident-workflows`, `incident-workflowbuilder`, and report resources 4526 through 4529.

Incident permissions are incident specific. A user's existing Student Transportation student, employee, or vehicle rights do not grant access to incidents involving those records. The `incident-*` resource grant is the gate.

School based access continues to apply on top of the resource grant. A user sees an incident when they hold the resource grant and have school access to a school that at least one involved student is assigned to. This is existing behavior and does not change.

A user without a grant on a subject resource does not see that subject anywhere in Incidents. The subject is absent from the subject selector, its area is unreachable, and incidents of that subject are excluded from lists, search, and dashboard counts, including incidents assigned to that user.

Acceptance criteria:

- Each seeded resource gates its corresponding area and honors the CRUD level of the grant
- A user with no grant on a subject resource cannot reach that area by direct URL
- The subject selector lists only subjects the user holds a create grant on
- Lists, search results, and dashboard counts exclude incidents whose subject the user holds no read grant on
- An incident assigned to a user is excluded when the user holds no read grant on its subject
- School based filtering applies after resource filtering, with behavior unchanged from today
- Grant changes take effect on next sign in, consistent with existing ST permission behavior

## 2. Complete the resource tree for the expanded subjects

Delivered under #193.

#191 expands incident subjects beyond students. Facility becomes Location and staff becomes Employee.

`incident-drivers` is renamed to `incident-employees`. In Student Transportation a driver is an Employee, so a separate driver resource would overlap the Employee subject. The resource is currently seeded with no grants and is not yet enforced, so the rename carries no data impact.

`incident-locations` is added as a new subject resource under the `incidents` parent.

Acceptance criteria:

- `incident-employees` exists in place of `incident-drivers`, nested under the `incidents` parent
- `incident-locations` exists, nested under the `incidents` parent
- Both carry `ResourcePermissionProperty` entries consistent with the other subject resources
- Both appear in the role permission tree under the `IncidentManagement` upgrade and are hidden when the upgrade is off
- Permission labels are present in `Permission.resx` and the es-US, fr-CA and ar-SA locale files
- Seeding remains additive and re-runnable

## 3. Default role grants for the subject areas

Delivered under #193.

The seed grants 56 permissions across Admin, Safety, Driver, Fleet and Principal, and leaves the subject areas and `incident-admin` ungranted. Ungranted plus the enforcement above means no role can reach those areas. Defaults are required.

Grants by resource, extending the split already established in the seed:

- `incident-students`: Admin full, Safety full, Principal read, Fleet none, Driver none
- `incident-employees`: Admin full, Safety full, Fleet read, Principal none, Driver none
- `incident-vehicles`: Admin full, Fleet full, Safety read and update, Principal none, Driver none
- `incident-locations`: Admin full, Safety full, Principal read, Fleet none, Driver none
- `incident-admin`: Admin full, all other roles none

These are shipped defaults. Districts change them in the role editor.

Acceptance criteria:

- A tenant with the upgrade enabled has the grants above present after the permission seed runs
- Each of the five default roles can reach exactly the areas listed and no others
- Re-running the seed adds no duplicate grants
- Existing grants are never edited or removed

## Out of scope

- The Employee Restricted permission layer
- Third party subject resources, deferred until a Student Transportation entity exists for third party
- Running `InsertDefaultIncidentPermission` at upgrade enable, tracked separately
- Any change to school based access filtering behavior

## Dependencies

- transportation-traversa#19960 must merge before this work starts
- #193 delivers blocks 2 and 3 in the Security DB seeding procs
- #176 is blocked on this issue
- #191 depends on #193

### Summary
Rider AI's General agent can look up runs, students, vehicles, employees, locations, rollouts, and scans — but **not incidents**. This adds incident/workflow data as a new set of **read-only MCP Resources** so users can query incident history, status, and workflow state conversationally. Read-only scope; conversational writes are tracked separately.

### Background & references
- **Rider AI V1 Scope:** https://tylertech.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/Transportation/pages/736330284
- **Rider AI Tools (naming conventions):** https://tylertech.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/Transportation/pages/736461362
- Authoritative incident schema, workflow model, and role/permission matrix live in this repo's incident service.

### Scope — Resources to add
Follow the documented `Identify* / List* / Get*ById` conventions; all land in the **General agent** (RiderAI-upgrade tier).

| Tool | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `IdentifyIncident` | resolve | "the fight on Bus 8 Tuesday" / "INC-2025-0064" → incident ID |
| `ListIncidents` | collection | Filter by status, type, severity, date range, route, school, driver, assignee |
| `GetIncidentById` | detail | Full record incl. involved students, witnesses, attachments, workflow state |
| `GetIncidentsForStudent / Driver / Vehicle / Route` | pivot | Relational history off existing entity keys |
| `GetWorkflowStatus` | detail | Current step, assigned role, pending approval, overdue vs. estimated duration |
| `ListPendingSteps` / `ListMyApprovals` | work-queue | Scoped to signed-in user's role |
| `GetParentNotificationStatus` | detail | Per involved student: notified flag + timestamp |

### Data contract
- Map each tool's output to the incident schema in this repo: incident core fields, `involvedStudents[]` (role: Instigator/Victim/Participant/Bystander, severity, parentNotified, actionTaken), `workflow` steps (assignedRole, status, order, requiresApproval, completedBy/Date).
- Confirm enum values: incident types, status (`Open/In Progress/Closed/Cancelled`), severity (`Low/Medium/High/Critical`).

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Tools return tool-backed data from the incident service; Rider does not guess when data is unavailable
- [ ] Results **respect existing Student Transportation permissions** (Driver = own only; Principal = read-only at their school; Admin/Safety Coordinator = broad)
- [ ] **Tenant isolation** enforced — no cross-district results
- [ ] Incident data handled as **FERPA education records**, consistent with current Rider data handling
- [ ] Gated behind the **RiderAI upgrade** entitlement / feature flag
- [ ] Map plotting works for incidents with coordinates (reuses GA map capability)
- [ ] Integration/eval tests pass for sample queries (open incidents by route; student incident history; "what's waiting on my approval?"; per-bus incident counts) and added to the Rider eval suite

### Out of scope
- Write/action tools (advancing steps, approvals, recording parent notification, conversational filing)

### Dependencies
- Incident service API/endpoints exposing records, workflow state, and involved-student detail (verify what exists vs. net-new)
- MCP tool-registration + the General agent's permission/tenant-filtering layer
- Permission mapping: ST roles → incident visibility

body:
If the Student Transportation site is in MDM mode, Incidents has to scope to organizations. It does none of that today. No incident table, no workflow table, and no incident configuration table carries an org, so on a multi-district site every district would see every other district's incidents.

The organization selector UI is split out to #198. This issue owns the data scoping and filtering.

## How Student Transportation already does MDM

The site-level switch is `IsMultiDistrictSite()`. When it is off, no org filter is applied anywhere and behavior is exactly what it is today.

There are two established conventions, and Incidents needs both:

- **Shared configuration** uses a companion association table named `<Entity>Org` holding `<Entity>Id` and `OrgKey`, filtered as `e.<Entity>Orgs.Any(x => orgs.Contains(x.OrgKey))`. Twenty-two entities already do this, including `GradeOrg`, `RunOrg`, `LocationOrg`, `EmployeeOrg` and `AssetOrg`.
- **Records owned by exactly one district** carry a scalar org key. `Student` carries `DistrictOrgKey` in addition to its `StudentOrg` rows.

`OrgFilterService` supplies the per-user org list through `GetUserOrgsAsync(userId)` and returns an unfiltered predicate when MDM is off, so the filter is a no-op on a single-district site.

## Every subject is already org-scoped

An incident does not need to be told its organization in most cases, because the entity it is about already knows:

- Student incidents derive from `Student.DistrictOrgKey`.
- Employee incidents derive from `EmployeeOrg`.
- Location incidents derive from `LocationOrg`.
- Vehicle incidents derive from `AssetOrg`. A vehicle is an `Asset` in Student Transportation, which is why `ApplyVehicleFilterAsync` is typed to `Asset`.

**Third Party is the one exception.** A third party incident names a person with no Student Transportation record, so there is nothing to derive from and the organization has to be captured when the incident is filed.

This is a better position than school-based access, where studentless incidents had nothing to derive from at all.

## Requirements

Incident records.

- An incident carries a single owning organization, following the `Student.DistrictOrgKey` convention rather than a join table, because an incident belongs to exactly one district.
- The organization is derived from the incident's subject on creation and is not asked for, except on a Third Party incident where the filer chooses it.
- On a Third Party incident, the organization defaults to the filer's organization when the filer has exactly one, and is a required choice when they have several.
- The organization cannot be changed after creation. Reassigning an incident across districts is out of scope.

Incident configuration.

- Incident types, workflows, workflow step templates and email templates each get an `<Entity>Org` association table, so a co-op can share one workflow across districts or scope one to a single district.
- Following the `<Entity>Org` naming convention matters beyond tidiness: `PopulateMDMEntities.sql`, the script that converts an existing single-district site to MDM, discovers association tables by querying `sys.tables` for names ending in `Org`. Named correctly, the conversion works with no change to that script.

Filtering.

- Every incident list, the dashboard, reports and communications filter to the user's organizations, using `GetUserOrgsAsync`.
- When MDM is off, no filter is applied and nothing about the UI changes.
- When a user has access to more than one organization, the incidents list shows the organization as a column and offers it as a filter.
- Selecting a student, employee, location or vehicle while filing is limited to entities in the user's organizations, so an incident cannot be created against an entity the filer cannot see.

Interaction with permissions.

- Organization scoping is applied in addition to the resource grants in #181, never instead of them. A user must both have access to the organization and hold the grant for the subject.
- School-based filtering from #190 applies within an organization, not across.

## Acceptance criteria

- With MDM off, every screen behaves exactly as it does today and no organization column or filter appears.
- With MDM on, a user with access to one organization sees only that organization's incidents on the list, the dashboard, reports and communications.
- A student, employee, location and vehicle incident each save with the organization derived from the subject, with no prompt.
- A third party incident requires an organization choice when the filer has more than one, and defaults silently when they have one.
- A user cannot select a student, employee, location or vehicle belonging to an organization they do not have.
- A workflow scoped to one organization is not offered on an incident in another.
- A user with the correct organization but without the #181 grant for a subject still cannot see those incidents.

## Still open

Whether a co-op wants incident types shared across districts by default or scoped per district by default. The association table supports either; only the seeded default has to be chosen.
title: MDM: Handle MDM in the UI/backend

Strategy for V2 here ## Dashboard Components (migrated from transportation-traversa) The following UI components feed data into this ticket's scope: - **Incident KPI Cards** — 5 Incident KPIs - **Incidents by Type Pie Chart** — Pie chart showing incidents by type - **Incidents by Vehicle Bar Chart** — Horizontal bar chart of incident count by vehicle *(note: per @Justin-Smith comment, "incidents by driver" was changed to vehicle)* - **Incidents by Day of Week Chart** — Vertical bar chart of incidents by day of the week
